description: Wire vectors of the OffsetFetch API (key 9, v0 to v9), replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: OffsetFetch request v2 that names its partitions explicitly, which is the request v0 and v1 have as well; only the version field of the header tells them apart.
OffsetFetch answer v2 for the committed partition: the same topics array the lower versions answer, and the group-level error code 0 appended after it.

OffsetFetch request v2 with a NULL topic array (ff ff ff ff), which asks the coordinator for every topic-partition the group has a committed offset for. Version 1 closes the connection on the same four bytes.
The answer to the null topic array: every committed topic-partition of the group, byte for byte the answer of the explicit request above.
OffsetFetch request v2 with an EMPTY topic array (00 00 00 00), which is a different request from the null one above: it names no topic at all.
The answer to the empty topic array of the same group: no topic and the error code 0, although the group has a committed offset.
OffsetFetch request v2 for a partition of the topic that the group never committed an offset for.
The answer for a partition without a committed offset: offset -1, EMPTY metadata (not null) and the error code 0, plus the group-level 0. Version 0 reports the error code 3 for the same case.

The shape of a group-level error of v2: an EMPTY topics array and the error code 16 (NotCoordinatorForGroup) after it, as OffsetFetchRequest.getErrorResponse() @ 0.10.2.2 builds it. Constructed, because the single-broker container coordinates every group itself and therefore never answers 14, 15, 16 or 30 - see the 'Broker quirks' note in the OffsetFetch section.

OffsetFetch request v1, which reads the offsets from the __consumer_offsets topic; the partitions are always explicit, the nullable topic array is version 2 of the api, which arrived with Kafka 0.10.2.
OffsetFetch response v1 reading back the offset that the OffsetCommit vector committed. There is no group-level error code after the topics array, which is the whole difference to v2.
OffsetFetch request v0, byte for byte the request of v1 with a lower version field; it reads the offsets from ZooKeeper.
OffsetFetch response v0 for a partition that the group never committed: offset -1 with the error code 3, which a client has to read as "no offset yet".
OffsetFetch request v3, byte for byte the frame of v2 with a higher version field.
The answer v3: the throttle time first, the topics, and then the group-level error code of v2.
OffsetFetch request v4 that names its partition explicitly, the frame of v2 and v3 with a higher version field.

The answer v4 reading back the offset the v4 commit stored: the throttle time, the topics, and the group-level error code that closes every answer from v2 on. The metadata of an offset committed without one is the EMPTY string, never null.
OffsetFetch request v5 (Kafka 2.1, KIP-320), byte for byte the frame of v2 to v4 with a higher version field: the change of this version is in the answer.
The answer v5 of the coordinator to the offset the v6 commit above stored: the partition entry now carries the `committed_leader_epoch` 0 between the committed offset and the metadata.

OffsetFetch request v6 (KIP-482): a compact group id and a compact topic array, which stays **nullable** in the flexible encoding - a `0` instead of the count asks for every topic the group committed.
The answer v6: the committed offset with the `committed_leader_epoch` of KIP-320 and a compact metadata string, and the group-level error code of version 2 behind the topic array.

OffsetFetch request v7 (Kafka 2.5, KIP-447): the flexible version 6 frame with one field more, the boolean `require_stable` behind the topic array - here `00`, false, which is what every version below 7 asks for implicitly.

The answer of that request while a transaction holds a newer offset for the very same partition: `require_stable = false` answers the **last stable** offset, 25, with the error code 0 - the pending 42 of the open transaction is not visible here and not an error either.
The same frame with `require_stable = true`, the `01` of KIP-447: the coordinator may only answer an offset no open transaction can still change.
The answer when nothing is pending: the committed offset 25 with the error code 0, byte for byte the answer of the request without the flag.
The same `require_stable = true` request once a transactional producer has written an offset for that partition without committing its transaction.

The answer that KIP-447 was written for: the partition carries the offset **-1**, an empty metadata and the **retriable** error code **88** `UnstableOffsetCommit`, while the group-level error code stays 0. A client waits and asks again; when the transaction has committed, the very same request answers the offset it wrote.

OffsetFetch request v8 (Kafka 3.0): the group id and the topic array of the versions below moved into the `groups` array, one entry per group, and the single `require_stable` of KIP-447 behind it holds for the whole batch. This one group names the partition 0 of `t3-30-vectors` explicitly.

The answer: the throttle time and one `groups` entry, which carries the group id, its topics and its own group-level error code. There is **no top-level error code** any more. The partition entry is the one of version 7, `committed_leader_epoch` included: the committed offset 25 (`19`), the epoch -1 of an offset that was committed without one, the empty metadata and the error code 0.

The same group with a **null** topic array - the compact `00` - which asks for every topic-partition the group has a committed offset for, exactly as the nullable array of version 2 does at the top level.
The answer is byte for byte the one of the explicit request, apart from the correlation id: the group has committed exactly this one partition.

Two groups in one request, which is what version 8 exists for: `t3-30-vectors-group`, which committed the offset 25, and `t3-30-vectors-other`, which the coordinator has never heard of. Both ask for the same partition.

One entry per group, in the order of the request. The known group answers its offset 25; the unknown one answers the offset -1 with the error code 0 in the partition **and** the group-level error code 0 - a group the coordinator does not know is not an error here either, exactly as it was at the top level of a version 2 answer.
The same one-group request with `require_stable = true` (`01` behind the array) while a transactional commit of that very partition is still open.

The **88** (UnstableOffsetCommit) of KIP-447 at version 8: the partition answers the offset -1, the empty metadata and the retriable code 88, while the group-level error code of the entry stays **0**. The flag and the code sit in the new shape exactly where they sat in the old one.

OffsetFetch request v9 (Kafka 3.7, KIP-848): the version 8 batch whose group entry gained a nullable `member_id` and a `member_epoch`, here at their defaults - the compact `00` of a null string and the four bytes `ff ff ff ff` of the epoch -1. This is the frame `Client::fetchGroupOffsets()` and `AdminClient::listGroupOffsets()` send for every read of a classic group.

The answer v9 of the committed offset 21: byte for byte the answer of version 8 - "the response is the same as version 8 but can return STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH and UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID errors when the new consumer group protocol is used".
The same read of the same **classic** group, with a member id the group never had and the epoch 7 in the two new fields.

The committed offset again: a classic group **ignores** both fields. `ClassicGroup::validateOffsetFetch` @ 3.9.2 takes the member id and the epoch and looks at neither - it only refuses a group in the state `Dead` - so neither the 25 nor the 113 can ever come out of one.
A group the coordinator has never heard of, asked at version 9 with a member id and an epoch.

The group-level code **0** and the offset -1 for the partition that was named: unlike OffsetCommit, whose version 9 answers the 69 `GroupIdNotFound`, OffsetFetch keeps the rule of every version below it. `OffsetMetadataManager::fetchOffsets` @ 3.9.2 catches the `GroupIdNotFoundException` of the lookup and fails every partition with the offset -1 instead - the member fields are never even looked at.

A member of a **KIP-848** group reading its own committed offset: the member id is the uuid the member generated for itself and the epoch is the one the coordinator answered its ConsumerGroupHeartbeat (key 68) with. The group was created on the node with a hand-built heartbeat - the api is the last wave of this line.
The code 0 and the offset 33: the member id and the epoch are the ones the coordinator holds.
The same member reading with the epoch below the one it holds.

The **113** `StaleMemberEpoch` of KIP-848, in the **group-level** error code of the entry, whose topic array is empty. An epoch *above* the current one is answered with the same 113, and so is the epoch **-1** as soon as a member id stands next to it: `ConsumerGroup::validateOffsetFetch` @ 3.9.2 skips the member lookup only when the id is null **and** the epoch is negative.
The same group asked with a member id it does not hold and the current epoch.

The **25** `UnknownMemberId`, the second code version 9 exists for, again at the group level and with an empty topic array. An **empty** member id - the `01` of a compact string of length 0 - is answered with the very same 25, because it is a member id like any other for the lookup.
The same KIP-848 group asked with the **null** member id of the default and an epoch that is not negative - a frame the specification allows and no client of the new protocol sends.

The **-1** `UnknownServerError`: `ConsumerGroup::validateOffsetFetch` @ 3.9.2 returns early only when the member id is null *and* the epoch is below zero, and looks the null id up in its member table otherwise, where `BaseHashTable::findSlot` dereferences the key. The group-level code is the int16 `ff ff` and the connection stays usable - the next request on it is answered normally.
The same member asking for **every** topic-partition its group committed an offset for: the compact `00` of the null topic array behind the member epoch.

The one partition the group has an offset for, named by the coordinator itself. The member is validated before the topics are collected, so this shape answers the 113 and the 25 exactly as the named one does.

The `require_stable` flag of KIP-447 (the `01` behind the group array) together with the member epoch: the two are independent, and the flag still holds for the whole batch while the member is named per entry.

The committed offset: no transaction of this partition is open. A stale epoch is answered with the 113 on this path as well, although the coordinator serves a `require_stable` read with a write operation of its own runtime rather than with a read one.

Two groups in one version 9 request: the classic group with the defaults of the two new fields and the KIP-848 member with a stale epoch. Every entry carries its own member, the one `require_stable` behind the array holds for both.

One entry per group, and the member validation is per entry as well: the classic group answers its offset with the code 0, the KIP-848 entry next to it the **113** with no topic at all. A bad member never costs the other groups of the batch their answer.
